'''Stephen Harry Crandall'''<ref>Elishakoff, I., “Stephen Harry Crandall”, in '''Encyclopedia of Continuum Mechanics''' (H.  Altenbach and A. Öchsner, eds.), pp. 465-468, Berlin: Springer, 2020.</ref> (December 2, 1920<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kH0-AQAAIAAJ&q=%22Crandall,+Stephen+Harry%22+AND+%221920%22 |title=Who's who in the World - Marquis Who's Who, LLC - Google Books |date= September 1976|publisher=Marquis Who's Who, Incorporated |isbn=9780837911038 |access-date=2013-11-02}}</ref> &ndash; October 29, 2013<ref>[http://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/2013/stephen-crandall-obituary-1108.html Stephen H. Crandall, professor emeritus in MechE, dies at 92]</ref>) was a professor of [[mechanical engineering]] at [[MIT]].   He earned his master's degree in engineering at [[Stevens Institute of Technology]] in [[Hoboken, New Jersey]] and his Ph.D. from MIT. He joined the MIT faculty in 1946 and taught dynamics and strength of materials until his retirement in 1991.  He was a prolific author of texts in [[solid mechanics]], numerical methods, and [[random vibration]].  His mentor at MIT was [[J. P. Den Hartog]].
He was awarded the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]] (ASME) [[Robert Henry Thurston Lecture Award]] in 1988<ref name="asme">{{cite web |title=Robert Henry Thurston Lecture Award |publisher=American Society of Mechanical Engineers |url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/robert-henry-thurston-lecture-award |access-date=June 14, 2026}}</ref> and the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers|ASME]] [[Timoshenko Medal]]<ref>{{cite web|author=iMechanica |url=http://www.imechanica.org/node/183 |title=1990 Timoshenko Medal Acceptance Speech by Stephen H. Crandall |publisher=iMechanica |date=2006-09-17 |access-date=2013-11-02}}</ref> in 1990  "in recognition of distinguished contributions to the field of applied mechanics."  He was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 1993.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/05/02/us/60-are-chosen-for-national-academy-of-sciences.html |title=60 Are Chosen for National Academy of Sciences |work=New York Times |date=1993-05-02 |access-date=2013-11-02}}</ref>
